job_title: Build an AI-Powered Customer Support Workflow with CRM Integration
subtitle: A practical implementation plan for customer support routing, AI assistance, CRM synchronization, and production monitoring.
engagement: Discovery and milestones to be confirmed

items: The job calls for a customer support workflow that can classify incoming requests, make relevant knowledge available to support agents, and synchronize ticket activity with the CRM.
A reliable implementation should account for escalation rules, customer context, permissions, response quality, and measurable outcomes rather than relying on AI responses alone.

sections.title: How the proposed skillset maps to your requirements

items.approach: Define supported ticket categories, confidence thresholds, and fallbacks to human review.
Map identifiers, authentication, event triggers, data contracts, and synchronization rules.
Include retries, audit logs, permissions, quality checks, and monitoring from the pilot stage.

items.title: Discovery and data review
items.description: Identify ticket channels, CRM fields, knowledge sources, priority rules, security constraints, and success metrics.

items.title: Solution design
items.description: Define the AI classification and retrieval design, API contracts, fallback behavior, and human approval points.

items.title: Pilot implementation
items.description: Connect one support channel to the chosen CRM and validate classification, enrichment, and handoff events.

items.title: Quality and failure testing
items.description: Test ambiguous tickets, sensitive information, outages, duplicate events, and low-confidence AI responses.

items.title: Rollout and handover
items.description: Deploy the approved workflow, establish monitoring, and document maintenance and escalation procedures.

items: Documented integration workflow and CRM field mappings
Configured ticket classification and routing logic within the agreed scope
Test plan covering common failures, escalations, and data handling
Deployment notes, operational monitoring checklist, and handover guide

Start with representative ticket categories and review the quality of classifications and CRM updates against agreed acceptance criteria. Roll out additional queues only after stakeholders approve the pilot.
Monitor unexpected model outputs, incorrect routing, retry behavior, access-control mistakes, and failed CRM synchronization.

rows.label: Working basis
rows.value: Milestone-based scope and acceptance criteria to be agreed.

rows.label: Initial step
rows.value: Review integration access, ticket samples, and the target CRM workflow.

items: Which helpdesk and CRM platforms, including versions, are in scope?
What data may be sent to the AI service, and what human review is required?
What ticket volumes and accuracy metrics should the pilot satisfy?

blocks.text: This document describes a proposed execution plan, not a claim of previously delivered work with any particular vendor.

closing: Thank you for considering this proposal.
